conclusions.point: Real math gap, not a missing model-named op
evidence: model_ops.h:1001-1045 forces F32 Q/K/W, F16 mask, F32 output and H64/D128
ggml.c:6459-6491 fixes F32 Q/W and F16 mask
tensor_program.cc:499-510/931-934; CPU provider:2067; Vulkan region:678; Metal native_program.cc:438 all call old ggml scorer
conclusions.finding: Widening official BF16 Q/K/W then calling old scorer omits BF16 dot/product/head-sum boundaries. Final-only BF16 cast cannot repair the chain.

conclusions.point: F16 mask is not the GA blocker
evidence: existing LightningIndexer mask broadcasts [Sm,1,T,L] across B
conclusions.finding: 0 and -Inf are exactly F16 representable. Generic nonzero finite additive-mask semantics would need explicit output-rounding definition; do not demand a new BF16-mask API solely for these GA profiles.

conclusions.point: Existing BF16 scorer math can be reused
conclusions.finding: All four implementations have BF16 dot output, BF16 weighted product and BF16 final head-sum then F32 widening. Current custom entry is Q[T,64,128], U8 row-inline bank[L,68], weights[T,64], I32 ranges: not dense official BF16 K. Packed/paged source access, safety and capture qualification must stay separate.

conclusions.point: Old native implementations have additional operand domains
evidence: CUDA lightning-indexer.cu:244-381 float vec path; F16/quantK path:~69-183 narrows Q/K to half before F32 WMMA
Metal kernels/fa.metal:2330-2423 always stages K/Q as half even for F32 K specialization
CPU ops.cpp:12105-12200 F32 dot/product/head sum; Vulkan lightning_indexer.comp:~100-153 F32 score accumulation
conclusions.finding: F32 accumulation is not a BF16 staged contract, nor universally F32 operands. Preserve old qualified behavior; do not silently advertise BF16 GA by broadening supports alone.

concrete_domains.missing: BF16 dot RNE before ReLU; BF16 product RNE before head reduction; BF16 head-sum RNE before mask/TopK; keep prescaled BF16 weights as actual operand, no moved head scaling
Dense BF16 cache / real strides. Existing packed Hyle FP4 bank cannot stand in for official BF16 QAT simulation cache, even though their finite decoded values may overlap.
Official start_pos=0 with S<compress_ratio yields L=0 and empty TopK output; LightningIndexer schema rejects L=0. Row-cache scorer already supports empty axes and checked ranges.

GA cache[:B,:L] is a prefix of [max_B,max_L,D]. With B>1 and L<max_L it has a padded batch stride, while public LightningIndexer only accepts dense descriptors. B1 active axes can be dense; do not infer every GA boundary is noncontiguous.

Both GA H64/D128 already match current scorer dimensions. Pro Top1024 and Flash Top512 are caller TopK policy, not a scorer hardware whitelist. Prefill -1 padding, offset and multi-rank all_reduce remain model/state/distributed composition, not evidence of a missing scorer primitive.

proposal.preferred: Use one typed score mathematical recipe/region based on actual dtype, not a GA/model-name branch. First express/reference with existing BF16 MatMul(F32 accumulation) -> BF16 ReLU -> BF16 Multiply -> ReduceSum(F32 accumulation, BF16 result), then mask and caller TopK. For efficient dense carrier, add a BF16 domain to the existing scorer or match this chain provider-locally; never route it to the unchanged old ggml scorer.
proposal.api: No new global precision knob or model-specific descriptor. Existing LightningIndexer can remain the old F32 domain; if it is extended, infer type/layout algebraically and version its explicit typed math contract. Same-typed operands and declared rounding are the discriminator; native H/D/layout limits belong in provider supports.
proposal.implementation: Reuse the current bounded-tile BF16 row-cache scoring core with dense BF16 key access, skipping packed decode. Keep decode, range/page permissions and token status in the existing packed wrappers. CPU ATen and Apple MLX already provide BF16 matmul/product/sum; CUDA reuses Lt plus existing typed pointwise/reduction kernels; Vulkan can share the explicit BF16 rounding arithmetic in its scorer shader.
proposal.qualification: Do not claim the ordinary chain is already supported on every backend: current Vulkan ggml View rejects BF16 and Cast to BF16 from F32 is declined (region.cc:599-623). Existing row-cache shader proves available arithmetic, not dense GA wiring. Each actual provider must implement or decline its typed/layout domain.

concrete_seams.scope: public math only if descriptor domain is expanded
concrete_seams.change: Define BF16 stage semantics inferred from actual operand dtype and version contract. No model/profile field; no broad support claim from infer alone.
Reuse current BF16 matmul/relu/product/sum helper on dense key tensors; real supports selects this path instead of old ggml F32 scorer.

Extract/reuse bounded tile Lt plus typed pointwise/reduction sequence with dense keys. Packed decoding/range validation remains in packed wrapper; no new CUDA arithmetic TU needed for initial math path.
Reuse BF16 MLX dot and explicit no-contraction finish on dense keys; do not send BF16 domain to half-staging ggml Metal Lightning kernel.
Share explicit BF16 arithmetic with a real dense-key access path, preserving actual strides/capacities. Existing packed shader is arithmetic evidence, not a ready dense entry.

minimal_tests: Reuse sparse_fragment_test_support as a layout/entry harness but replace its dyadic F32-only values with BF16 post-QAT-boundary witnesses; its existing all-ones case cannot detect this gap.

Reuse row_cache_indexer_fixture.expected(true) vs expected(false) and decode its tiny finite keys to dense BF16 without relabeling the encoded artifact. Add staged dot/product/head-sum witnesses, NaN/ReLU classification, negative weights and mask 0/-Inf.

One tiny B1 dense two-slot/rebind/capture case; one B>1 padded-prefix case must either be correctly supported or explicitly rejected; L=0 must return empty outputs without payload reads. Preserve range/page/accepted-error tests in their existing wrappers.

Use independent staged operations for numeric oracle; do not demand arbitrary full-model bitwise Torch identity because the fixed model.py does not prescribe dot or head-sum reduction tree. TopK tied membership/order needs separate defined comparison.
limits: No definite new small correctness bug was established in the existing BF16 row-cache scorer; it already preserves NaN and staged boundaries. The old Lightning F32/native variants are not being rewritten under an unstated GA contract.
The source establishes visible BF16 tensor boundaries; exact physical Torch accumulation/reassociation and distributed all_reduce algorithm are not established by model.py.
No whole GA, artifact, GGUF cache codec or all-eight-model runtime journey was validated.
